subject: Client success transition: implementation plan & cost/perf tuning
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Turner <elise@finatra.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Client success transition: implementation plan & cost/perf tuning

Hi Elise —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As discussed, we want to kick off a short, focused implementation sprint that ensures Finatra meets its latency SLOs while keeping unit costs predictable. I’m looping in Monica (CS) and Rishi (Platform) to own execution and model/config details.

High-level goals for the first two sprints (2 weeks):
- Verify p95 latency <= 200ms for the 512-token checkout path
- Reduce per-1000-token serving cost 15% vs the baseline via batching/caching/quant profiles
- Deploy safe routing policy so production traffic falls back to a lower-cost variant during peak load

Key deliverables we propose:
1) Baseline capture: sample traces + prefix distributions from your staging traffic (attach CSV below)
2) Quant & kernel recommendations: quick A/B of int8 vs fp16-like profile on your 1B/3B candidates
3) Batching/caching config: target batch sizes for 95th% latency constraint, and KV prefix caching policy for repeated prompts
4) Routing policy: policy spec for primary/secondary model variants, with circuit-breaker thresholds

Attachments: finatra_prefix_latency_samples.csv (small extract), proposed_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft)

Can you confirm the top two production paths we should prioritize (e.g., checkout flow, search snippet generation), and whether there are any hard constraints on tokenization or privacy we should observe?

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Wed 10am PT to finalize the mutual action plan. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and assign owners.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Elise Turner <elise@finatra.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finatra.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Client success transition: implementation plan & cost/perf tuning

Thanks Karthik — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

- Priority paths: 1) Checkout UX (user-facing completion with product suggestions) — this must meet p95 <= 200ms; 2) Admin summarization for support tickets (less sensitive, can be slower up to 500ms).
- Throughput expectations: 150 reqs/min average now, peaks ~450 reqs/min during promos. We expect load to grow 2-3x over the next quarter.
- Model constraints: we plan to use the open-3B family for production; evals on the 1B were acceptable but lacked some answer richness.
- Data/privacy: customer PII is redacted upstream by our app, so you can work with sampled payloads; we’ll keep the sampling window to three days.

Wed 10am PT works. I’ll add Daniel for any infra notes.

—Elise
Elise Turner
Head of Product, Finatra
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Turner <elise@finatra.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Client success transition: implementation plan & cost/perf tuning

Elise / team — great, thanks for the quick reply and the priorities. I’ll lead the CS side and run the two-week plan. For visibility I’m pasting a concise mutual action plan below (we’ll upload an editable spreadsheet to the Drive link).

MUTUAL ACTION PLAN (two 1-week sprints)
Week 1 — Baseline & Quick Wins
- Owner: Monica / Finatra (Elise)
- Tasks: provide 3-day sampled traces (CSV), confirm tokenization/version, agree on primary model (open-3B).
- Redwood deliverables: initial batching matrix, KV prefix cache recommendation, quantization safety checklist (int8 smoke tests).

Week 2 — Validate & Deploy
- Owner: Rishi / Redwood infra
- Tasks: run small A/B calls on staging (int8 vs fp16-like), validate p95 latency at target batch sizes, configure routing policy with primary/secondary variants and fallback thresholds.
- Redwood deliverables: rollout checklist, automated fallback rule, cost delta report (expected per-1k tokens).

Questions for your Wed call so we can come prepared:
1) Can you share a small set of representative prompt templates for checkout (examples only)?
2) Are there any endpoints that must never be quantized (e.g., legal text generation)?
3) Can we get a single staging endpoint that mirrors your production traffic shape for 24 hours?

Proposed owners on Redwood: Monica (CS lead), Rishi (platform/infra), Markus (model/quant advisor). I’ll create tasks in the shared Drive and HubSpot (HS-83712).

Thanks — I’ll send the 10am PT invite shortly.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finatra.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Elise Turner <elise@finatra.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Client success transition: implementation plan & cost/perf tuning

Monica — quick note ahead of the sync: we can provide sample prompt templates and a 24-hour staging dump on Thursday. One ask: our legal team flagged that any quantization that changes determinism on regression-critical prompts could affect our downstream A/B tracking. Can we get a safety gate that keeps deterministic outputs for specified templates?

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Cho
Engineering Manager, Finatra
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Turner <elise@finatra.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finatra.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Client success transition: implementation plan & cost/perf tuning

Daniel / Elise — noted — we have a couple of options for that safety gate:
1) Template-level policy: mark prompt templates as "deterministic-only" and force fp16-like execution path for those requests.
2) Regression harness: run a regression test during the A/B that compares outputs for flagged prompts and rejects quantized rollout if divergence exceeds threshold.

We’ll bring a short decision matrix to the sync (10am PT) and a proposed rollout with a 10% canary step and automated rollback thresholds based on output divergence + latency.

See you on the call — invite in your calendars.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform | Redwood Inference
